policy.description: Blocking line-coverage ratchets. Update measured counts in the same reviewed change whenever scope or coverage advances; never lower a floor without an explicit, justified scope change.

tolerance.rationale: The #369 body-observer ownership fix adds one instrumented and covered client/core line so stale handles compare their exact subscriber identity before cleanup, advancing the reviewed high-water from 2326/2666 (87.247%) to 2327/2667 (87.252%). Two clean Node 22.20/V8 runs on 2026-07-27 each passed all 1788 tests across 233 files and reproduced exactly 2327/2667. Retaining the existing one-line tolerance makes the minimum 2326/2667 (87.214%), stricter than the prior 2325/2666 tolerated floor (87.209%). coverage-baseline.test.js retains the exact below-floor, above-baseline, scope-change, and broad-tolerance negative boundaries.

EP-01.5 (#508) adds the host-adapter seam: IPlatformHost with its IHostUsers/IHostLibrary/IHostSessions/IHostPlugins facets, the kernel-owned HostUser/HostItem/HostSession/HostPlugin types, and the single JellyfinPlatformHost adapter, moving the instrumented scope from 36,336 to 36,405 lines. The adapter is reached in tests through an internal delegate seam rather than by faking Jellyfin's manager interfaces, which are far too large to implement; that keeps every mapping verified instead of permanently uncovered, and the mappings are where this type's defects would live. JellyfinPlatformHostTests covers each translation, including the two that silently corrupt meaning if they regress: an item or session with no owner must report null rather than Guid.Empty, which would otherwise read as a real all-zeroes id, and a plugin's status must come from its manifest, with a disabled plugin reporting Restart because Jellyfin never unloads an assembly (EP-00 spike-evidence S5/S6). PlatformHostSeamTests enforces the seam against the source in the AtomicFileWriteGuardTests style, with an allowlist of one file, an anti-rot test, a reflection test proving no seam signature exposes a host type, and a proof that the scan is non-vacuous. It judges code with comments stripped, so the seam's own documentation may name the type it excludes; the stripper is itself tested, including the case where naive handling of a URL's slashes would hide a real violation. The guard was negative-tested: a planted host reference in PlatformConstants.cs failed by name. Nine clean .NET 10.0.9/Coverlet runs on 2026-07-28 each passed all 2,387 tests at the same 36,405-line scope and measured 27,687 covered lines five times, 27,688 twice and 27,689 twice, so the reviewed high-water is 27,689 (76.058%). The observed spread was only two lines, but the tolerance is held at five rather than narrowed to match, because earlier scopes in this same repository showed spreads of five and six lines and CI hardware differs from the machine sampled here; narrowing to the luckiest observed window would convert ordinary Coverlet jitter into red builds. The floor still rises to 27,684/36,405 (76.039%) from the prior 27,623/36,336 (76.021%), and the tolerance narrows from six lines to five, so the ratchet tightens in both directions. coverage-baseline.test.js retains the exact scope-drift, regression, stale-baseline, and broad-tolerance negative boundaries.
